solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rid oneself of sin? This woman won't

parts.note: to shed something is to get rid of it
sin is evil, wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A question about repentance, answered by pointing at a woman who refuses to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a wicked woman is the one who won't 'shed evil'. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a malicious, wicked woman, exactly the kind who would never give up her wickedness.

clue.text: Spices up The Times?

definitions.meaning: to season food is to add spice to it
times of year; the question mark flags the newspaper misdirection

explanation.surface: The newspaper livening itself up with a bit of spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasons is both a verb for flavouring food and a plural noun for periods of the year.

clue.text: Priest regularly dropping bits of éclair

indicators.note: losing every other letter of the pastry's name leaves the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A clergyman leaving crumbs of pastry behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel, a crossword regular.

clue.text: Anxious the exercising may cause great fatigue?

indicators.note: putting the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: Worrying that a workout will leave one shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' seems to describe the anxious person but signals the anagram of ANXIOUS THE; 'may cause' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion is extreme tiredness, a state of being completely drained.

clue.text: Realise time's running out for northerner

indicators.note: a time running out is gone, so one of its letters leaves the word

parts.note: to intuit is to realise by instinct
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone becoming aware that their time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running out' removes one T from INTUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous people of the Arctic, so an Inuit is someone from the far north.

clue.text: A report of playwright on the beach?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the clue gives what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A news item about a dramatist seen by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'a Shaw' and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land rather than at sea, as one is when standing on the sand.

clue.text: Broadcast not originally by Empress of Blandings?

parts.note: the Empress of Blandings is Lord Emsworth's prize pig in P G Wodehouse's Blandings novels, a sow

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first one

explanation.surface: An aristocratic figure kept off the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside, putting N after SOW. Wodehouse's Empress is a prize pig, not royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that is broadcast is scattered widely by hand, that is, sown.

clue.text: Foolishly threaten cop? You might find yourself here

indicators.note: acting foolishly is acting wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Threaten a policeman and you will end up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as the consequence: threatening a cop lands you in trouble, which the anagram of THREATEN COP spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the carpet is an idiom for being summoned for a reprimand, where a foolish offender would end up.

clue.text: Slip between the sheets?

parts.note: a correction slip is inserted among the pages of a printed book; the surface suggests going to bed

explanation.surface: Getting into bed, or something more illicit.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, often listed on a separate slip tucked into a book's leaves.

clue.text: Member of nobility considers swallowing tablets

indicators.note: something swallowed goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: if something counts, it is considered to matter; to count is to consider
ES is slang for ecstasy tablets, E being one pill

explanation.surface: An aristocrat deciding whether to take her pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A countess is a noblewoman, the wife of an earl or count or holding that rank herself.

clue.text: One who's uncomfortable, absentee from school perhaps

definitions.meaning: someone ill at ease in unfamiliar surroundings
a fish missing from its school, a group of fish, would be out of the water

explanation.surface: A pupil playing truant and feeling awkward about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person out of their element, while literally a fish separated from its school.

clue.text: Rotten placement? That's discouraging

parts.note: food that is rotten has gone off
putting something somewhere is placing it

explanation.surface: A poor job of positioning something leaves people disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off-putting is unappealing and deters people, so it is discouraging.

clue.text: Some might say it's Adam or I, grammatically speaking

definitions.meaning: in the Bible story Adam was the first human
the pronoun I is the ... singular in grammar

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about naming oneself as Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the earliest human being and the grammatical category of the speaker.

clue.text: Join police around end of June

indicators.note: one piece is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Signing up to the police force at the close of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that meet come together, so they join.

clue.text: Study cites ruins in Byzantine state

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are put into a tangled order

explanation.surface: An archaeologist referencing the ruins of the Byzantine empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine' looks like the historical empire but works as the anagram signal on CITES RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise is to examine closely, to study carefully.

clue.text: School acquiring oddly neglected Scarlatti score

indicators.note: the school takes in the other letters, so they go inside it
neglecting the odd letters keeps only the even ones

explanation.surface: A music school picking up a forgotten Scarlatti composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical but means a mark; 'oddly neglected' leaves CRAT from Scarlatti.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a surface is to score it, marking it with a line.

clue.text: Incomplete clue for party?

definitions.meaning: a party is a DO, which is half of the letters of DONE, so the phrase could clue it

explanation.surface: An unfinished hint about a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-done means only partly finished, and read as wordplay it is a crossword-style clue for a party.

clue.text: Allegation by old flame will make you cry

indicators.note: placed beside, here with the former partner coming first

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: An accusation from a former lover will reduce you to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cry' looks like weeping but means calling out; 'will make you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, as in surprise.

clue.text: Stolen ring returned in spring

parts.note: stolen goods are slang hot

indicators.note: something returned goes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a loop is a ring shape

explanation.surface: A stolen ring handed back in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but means a natural source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pool is a natural thermal spring where heated groundwater gathers.

clue.text: A close relation? Do him in if misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave run out of line, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A murderous threat against a family member who acts up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A close relation' suggests a relative; the question mark flags that it means kin to humans in evolutionary terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominids are the great apes and humans, so a hominid is one of humanity's nearest kin.

clue.text: Bamboozled, as a bat may be?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman, or bat, is ... when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground

explanation.surface: A confused flying bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumped means utterly baffled, and is also a way a cricket batsman is dismissed.

clue.text: Send mad Commie back, row initially avoided

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a commie, a communist, is a red

indicators.note: the first letter is skipped, so it is dropped

parts.note: a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A communist driven to madness after dodging an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RED to DER; 'initially avoided' drops the R of RANGE to leave ANGE. 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone is to drive them insane, unhinging their mind.

clue.text: Auditor's humble appearance

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is the word as heard

parts.note: mean can describe something humble or lowly, as in mean dwellings

explanation.surface: An accountant with a modest look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their outward appearance.

clue.text: A nurse covering up daughter's conduct

indicators.note: the outer pieces hide the daughter from view, enclosing her

parts.note: to minister to the sick is to nurse them
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A nurse concealing what a daughter did.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation or a test is to conduct or manage it.

clue.text: How spam comes from South America in the past

definitions.meaning: Spam, the tinned meat, comes in a can

definitions.text: from South America in the past
definitions.meaning: Relating to the Inca empire of the Andes

explanation.surface: Tinned meat of South American origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes the pre-Columbian empire of Peru, and split in two it says the meat is packed in a tin.

clue.text: Attention! Bishop turning up in Glasgow bank

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means read bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop arriving at a Scottish bank at a call to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank, as by a river.

clue.text: Old and cowardly, with an absence of bounce

parts.note: no means none, an absence
spring is bounce or elasticity
chicken means cowardly

explanation.surface: Describing an elderly, timid person who has lost their energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone no longer young.

clue.text: Squawking Antipodean I ignored in chain store

indicators.note: the letter is passed over, so it is dropped

parts.note: Ikea is the Swedish furniture store chain

explanation.surface: A noisy Australian shopping in a furniture chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antipodean' suggests a person but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a loud New Zealand mountain parrot, a bird from the Antipodes.

clue.text: Book that might be written by Defoe?

definitions.meaning: A book of the Old Testament
... Defoe, author of Robinson Crusoe, would sign his first name

explanation.surface: A volume attributed to the novelist Defoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a biblical book and the first name Defoe would write as part of his signature.

clue.text: Excessive anger, leaving university too young

indicators.note: something leaving goes out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: undue means excessive
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A student storming out of university in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes one U out of UNDUE to give UNDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Underage describes someone below the legal age, so too young for something.
